name: P2b - Heartbeat watcher (alerts once per stall)

nodes.name: Every 5 Minutes
nodes.notes: Keep the watcher in a DIFFERENT workflow from the job it watches: a dead job cannot report its own death.

nodes.name: Config
nodes.notes: Put YOUR alert webhook here (for example a Slack incoming webhook). It is a secret: keep it in this one node and never share a file that contains the real value.

nodes.name: Check heartbeats

parameters.query:
SELECT j.job,
       COALESCE(h.last_run_at, 'epoch'::timestamptz) AS last_run_at,
       round(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - COALESCE(h.last_run_at, 'epoch'::timestamptz))) / 60) AS stale_mins
FROM (VALUES ('release_tasks', interval '45 minutes')) AS j(job, max_age)
LEFT JOIN job_heartbeat h ON h.job = j.job
LEFT JOIN job_alert_state a ON a.job = j.job
WHERE COALESCE(h.last_run_at, 'epoch'::timestamptz) < now() - j.max_age
  AND (a.alerted_at IS NULL
       OR a.alerted_at <= COALESCE(h.last_run_at, 'epoch'::timestamptz)
       OR a.alerted_at < now() - interval '2 hours');

nodes.notes: Deliberately NO Always Output Data: a healthy or already-alerted job returns 0 rows, and that empty output is what stops the chain. Turning it on would alert on every run. Read-only SELECT, so the retry is safe. If this query itself fails, the error item reaches 'Build alert' and is reported as 'could not check', never as a stall.

nodes.name: Build alert
nodes.notes: Source with comments: code/p2b-build-alert.js. Edit the JOBS map for your own jobs.

nodes.name: Send alert
nodes.notes: Retry is safe: a duplicate alert is better than a lost one. Slack-style incoming webhooks answer the text 'ok'; the next node only records the alert as delivered when it sees that.

nodes.name: Mark alert sent

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO job_alert_state (job, alerted_at, detail)
SELECT $1::text, now(), 'stall alert delivered'
WHERE $2::boolean AND COALESCE($1::text, '') <> ''
ON CONFLICT (job) DO UPDATE SET alerted_at = now(), detail = EXCLUDED.detail
RETURNING job;

nodes.notes: Writes only when the webhook answered 'ok' AND the alert was a real stall (never for a failed check, which would silence a real stall for 2 hours). Idempotent upsert, so the retry is safe. If this write fails, the worst case is one duplicate alert at the next check, never a lost one.
